$note: Declarative per-package layer overrides for docs/architecture/layering.md, consumed by scripts/architecture/check-layer-deps.mjs. It exists because a packages/<group>/ directory can span several layers: packages/core/ is described in packages/README.md as 'Product API spine: sessions, prompts, tools, agent services, and the concrete loop' -- the spine and the loop are different layers in the same group, and no group-directory rule can separate them. Entries here outrank the group fallback and are outranked by nothing. This file was authored and committed BEFORE the checker was next run against it, so no entry can have been chosen to make a violation count fall; a later edit that moves a package must carry its own stated reason in $changeLog.

$authorship.basis: each package's stated purpose in packages/core/README.md and the layer definitions in docs/architecture/layering.md

@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop.reason: The layer definition names 'the agent loop' outright.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-tool-presentation.reason: Composes one agent's tools; composition is what this layer is.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt.reason: An assembly registry -- a seam others register into.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope.reason: A shared primitive with no capability logic and no provider.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent.reason: RECORDED ROLE CONFLICT, resolved in favour of the frozen Contract stage rather than quietly picked. By its own description -- 'Agent interface, registry, initiator scope, and event vocabulary' -- this package reads as capability-definitions: a seam implementors register into. But scripts/architecture/layer-order.ts's KNOWN_PACKAGE_LAYERS, frozen and ACCEPTED at P0-04's Contract stage, pins it at orchestration-runtime, and a Usage stage does not overturn an accepted Contract stage. The underlying fact is that the package carries both the Agent seam definition and the runtime registry, which belong to different layers; that is a split proposal for a later stage, not something this map should paper over.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-session.reason: STRADDLES LAYERS; the signer predicted in advance that no single answer is correct here. 'Event-sourced session store' is an implementation (providers), yet SessionEvent/SessionHeader are consumed repo-wide as vocabulary (protocol-types) -- definition and implementation in one package. The value here is its first-named role in that description, chosen by a stated rule rather than by result: the primary role the package's own description leads with. Violations that survive this assignment are evidence the package straddles layers, per the prediction recorded before the run, and the answer to those is a split proposal or a dated owned allowlist entry -- never another pass over this table.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.reason: STRADDLES LAYERS; predicted in advance like dsh-session. 'Tool registry and execution pipeline' -- the registry is a seam (capability-definitions), the pipeline is runtime (orchestration-runtime), in one package. Assigned by the same stated rule: the first-named role in the package's own description. Surviving violations are evidence of straddling, not of a table still needing tuning.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team.reason: A profile is an assembly (signed composition-root table).
A profile is an assembly (signed composition-root table).
Signed composition-root table: the agent-team runtime itself, not its profile.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-.reason: Signed composition-root table: a UI plugin.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-client-runner.reason: DIRECTORY MISFIT, same treatment and same reasoning as @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-cordis: a client-surface package living under packages/extensions/. It depends on client-ui-renderer, client-ui-theme, client-modules and api-remotes, which is what a client surface does, not what a runtime extension does. Signed by the coordinator delegate on 2026-09-04 after the Writer declined to classify it while looking at the violation counter. No directory move: a move touches imports, tsconfigs, the lockfile and the catalog, which is disproportionate to a classification problem. This entry is the input for later directory hygiene.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-cordis.reason: DIRECTORY MISFIT, and the comment is the finding: this is a UI card living under packages/extensions/. Its own description is 'Cordis dynamic-plugin definition card: the keyed cordis_define tool row with its run/stop switch' and its npm name is @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-cordis, so it is a presentation surface by both its name and its own account; only its directory says otherwise, which is why the packages/client rule does not reach it. A per-package entry is used deliberately INSTEAD of moving the directory: a move touches imports, tsconfigs, the lockfile and the catalog, which is a broad refactor for a classification problem and disproportionate to P0-04. This entry is the input for whoever later does directory hygiene.

$authorship2.scope: the composition-root table: packages/bundle/*, apps/*, and the four experimental/extensions packages below
$authorship2.basis: which packages depend on a bundle: nothing under packages/ does except another bundle (dsh-web-app, dsh-base, dsh-acp-app are depended on only by apps/cli; dsh-sdk-app only by apps/cli and packages/bundle/sdk-minimal). Established before any violation count was consulted.
$authorship2.prediction: If the 89 orchestration-runtime -> surfaces-apps edges largely vanish once composition-root exists, the classification was wrong and clearing them is correct. Anything that survives is a real finding, handled by a split proposal or a dated allowlist entry with a named owner. No third pass over this table.

$authorship3.scope: packages/client/** -- SUPERSEDES the per-package client rule signed earlier the same day
$authorship3.rule: packages/client/** -> surfaces-apps, all of it, including the six non-ui-* members
$authorship3.withdrawnRuleVerbatim: The signer attempted to layer client/ by self-described role (2026-09-04); the measurement returned a net +12 upward edges. A self-description covers half of what these packages are. The group is one horizontal layer, not a vertical stack. This conclusion was produced by measurement, not chosen by the classifier.
$authorship3.counterexamples: client/locale calls itself an extensible catalogue yet depends on four ui-* packages; client/connection calls itself an RPC transport yet depends on host-webserver and tool-todo; client/web calls itself a boot kernel yet depends on ui-primitives/ui-renderer/ui-slots, and something that assembles UI cannot sit beneath it.
$authorship3.supersededMeasurement: The earlier per-package client rule cleared 9 edges and created 12 (143 -> 146). That refutation is what produced this ruling.
$authorship3.uiStarCountCorrection: The first client table said 'all 40 ui-* packages'; the real count is 38. Recorded rather than silently corrected. The superseding rule matches the whole group, so the count no longer bears on it.

$authorship4.scope: packages/test-support/** excluded from the ranked production dependency graph
$authorship4.criterion: A test-support package's job is to assemble the thing under test, so it must depend on it; and no production package depends on it. Same reasoning as composition-root, and it carries the same second half: any ranked package depending on test-support/** is a violation (test-support-inbound-dependency), proven by mutation in both directions. An exclusion without the reverse constraint would cancel a constraint rather than add one.
$authorship4.correctionThatProducedIt: The Writer reported that packages/test-support/client-runtime carried 'hard dependencies (not devDependencies)' on six production UI packages. That was wrong and was checked before relaying: dependencies has 3 entries, all third-party (@testing-library/dom, @testing-library/react, vitest), and zero DSH packages; the 17 UI/API edges are peerDependencies mirrored in devDependencies per the repo's peer+dev convention. The edge is real under the declared production edge set, but the package does not bundle production UI, and with that corrected the composition-root reasoning applies unchanged.
